raw_response:
I am already old, so I do not want to spread myself too thin. Cotton is still my main crop this year because I know how to manage it, and on our side many people still plant it when they have well water. But I will not put all 18 mu into cotton. Cotton ties up the land for a long time and needs many hands when picking. Some people in my family work outside, so labor is not always there. I will keep most land in cotton, and leave a smaller piece in wheat followed by summer maize. That way I have steadier grain in the house and do not rely on one crop only. I do mostly what worked before. I do not dare cut fertilizer too much, because if the crop turns weak later, making up yield is hard. But I also cannot spend wildly, so I use moderate amounts, not the heaviest rates.

For cotton, I will plant the larger part, use the usual local hybrid seed, put fertilizer once at planting and once later when the plants are growing strong. If water is short, I save irrigation for the more important times, around seedling establishment and flowering-boll setting. For wheat, I sow a small area in October like usual, then after harvest I rush to plant maize on the same land. That wheat-maize piece is mainly for security. The turnaround is tight, so I keep tillage simple and do not do fancy things. If pests are light, I spray only when I see a real problem. This year I am aiming for a stable crop, not chasing the highest yield.
